# `silk/git/remote`

<!-- Generated by silk doc-reference. Do not edit by hand. -->

List the branches, tags, and other references of a remote Git repository over HTTP or HTTPS,
like `git ls-remote`.

## When to use
Call [`GitRemote.listRefs`](#GitRemote.impl.listRefs) with the URL of a repository, such as
`https://github.com/silk-lang/silk.git`, to get its references as a `RefList` from
`silk.git.refs`. Then look up a branch or a tag, or find the default branch with
`RefList.head`. Narrow the list with [`ListOptions.prefix`](#ListOptions.impl.prefix), such as `refs/tags/`, which large
repositories answer much faster. The request goes through the `Http` service of
`silk.http.client`, so tests can give a fake server.

## Details
It speaks the smart HTTP protocol of Git. By default it asks for protocol version 2 and sends an
`ls-refs` command with the prefixes, so the server filters the list. A server that answers with
version 0 sends all references in its first response, and the list is filtered on the client.
A dumb HTTP server, which serves the `info/refs` file, is read too. For each annotated tag the
result has the peeled object, and `HEAD` has the default branch as its target when the server
reports it. Redirects of the first request are followed, and the second request goes to the
URL that the first one ended at.

The functions [`GitRemote.parseAdvertisement`](#GitRemote.impl.parseAdvertisement), [`GitRemote.parseLsRefs`](#GitRemote.impl.parseLsRefs), and
[`GitRemote.parseDumbRefs`](#GitRemote.impl.parseDumbRefs) read a response body that you got another way.

## Errors
- `GitRefError` from `silk.git.refs` if the response is not a reference advertisement, is
  malformed, or is an `ERR` packet from the server.
- `HttpError` from `silk.http.client` if the request fails or the status is not from 200 to
  299. A private repository without credentials usually answers 401 or 404.
- `OutOfMemoryError` if the `Allocator` fails.

## Gotchas
The URL is used as given, so it must be the repository URL that `git clone` accepts, without
`/info/refs`. Only HTTP and HTTPS URLs work, not SSH or `git://`. For a private repository, set
the `Authorization` header with [`ListOptions.authorization`](#ListOptions.impl.authorization), such as `Basic` with a token.

## Examples
### List the tags of a repository from a fake server
```silk
import silk.mem.allocator { Allocator, OutOfMemoryError }
import silk.core.effect { Effect }
import silk.collections.list { List }
import silk.core.option { Option }
import silk.core.result { Result }
import silk.git.refs { GitRefError, Ref }
import silk.git.remote { GitRemote, ListOptions }
import silk.http.client { Http, HttpError, Request, Response }

struct DumbServer {}

impl Http for DumbServer {
  effect fn sendAll(self: &mut Self, requests: List<Request<'_>>) -> List<Result<Response, HttpError>>
    ! OutOfMemoryError
    ? &mut Allocator {
    return run Http.sendEach(move requests) |> Effect.provideMut<Http>(&mut self.*)
  }

  effect fn send(self: &mut Self, request: Request<'_>) -> Response
    ! HttpError | OutOfMemoryError
    ? &mut Allocator {
    return run Response.make(200, b"95d09f2b10159347eece71399a7e2e907ea3df4f\trefs/tags/v1.0.0\n")
  }
}

effect fn tagged() -> bool ! GitRefError | HttpError | OutOfMemoryError ? &mut Http | &mut Allocator {
  let mut options = ListOptions.make()
  run options.prefix("refs/tags/")
  let refs = run GitRemote.listRefs("https://git.example.com/app.git", &options)
  return match refs.resolve("v1.0.0") {
    Option<&Ref>.Some { value } => value.isTag()
    Option<&Ref>.None => false
  }
}

pub effect fn main() -> i32 ! GitRefError | HttpError | OutOfMemoryError {
  let mut allocator = Allocator.systemAllocatorProvider()
  let mut server = DumbServer {}
  let found = run tagged() |> Effect.provideMut<Http>(&mut server)
    |> Effect.provideMut<Allocator>(&mut allocator)
  if found {
    return 0
  }
  return 1
}
```

<a id="GitProtocol.Version2"></a>

### `Version2`

```silk
Version2
```

Ask for version 2, and fall back to version 0 when the server does not speak it. The server
filters the references by prefix. This is the default.

<a id="GitProtocol.Version0"></a>

### `Version0`

```silk
Version0
```

Ask for version 0 only. The server sends all references in one response, and the client
filters them.

<a id="ListOptions"></a>

## `ListOptions`

```silk
pub struct ListOptions
```

What [`GitRemote.listRefs`](#GitRemote.impl.listRefs) asks for: the prefixes of the names to list, the credentials, the
protocol, and the body limit.

### Details

[`ListOptions.make`](#ListOptions.impl.make) lists every reference with protocol version 2, no credentials, and a limit
of [`DEFAULT_MAX_BODY_BYTES`](#DEFAULT_MAX_BODY_BYTES) for each response body. A reference is listed when its full name
starts with one of the prefixes, or always when there are none. So `refs/tags/` lists the tags
and `refs/heads/` the branches. `HEAD` is listed only with no prefixes or with a prefix that it
starts with, such as `HEAD`.

<a id="ListOptions.impl.prefix"></a>

### Method `prefix`

```silk
pub effect fn prefix(self: &mut Self, prefix: string) -> ()
    ! OutOfMemoryError
    ? &mut Allocator
```

Adds `prefix` to the prefixes of the names to list, such as `refs/tags/` or `refs/heads/`.

#### Details

A reference is listed when its full name starts with any of the prefixes. The comparison is of
bytes, so `refs/heads/v` also matches `refs/heads/v2-dev`.

#### Errors

- `OutOfMemoryError` if the `Allocator` cannot supply the copy of `prefix`.

<a id="GitRemote.impl.listRefs"></a>

### Associated function `listRefs`

```silk
pub effect fn listRefs(url: string, options: &ListOptions) -> RefList
    ! GitRefError | HttpError | OutOfMemoryError
    ? &mut Http | &mut Allocator
```

Returns the references of the repository at `url` that `options` selects, like
`git ls-remote`.

#### Details

It sends `GET <url>/info/refs?service=git-upload-pack`. With protocol version 2, it asks for
version 2 in the `Git-Protocol` header. When the server answers with version 2, it then sends
`POST <url>/git-upload-pack` with an `ls-refs` command that has the prefixes and asks for
peeled tags and symbolic targets. A server that answers with version 0 or 1 lists all
references in its first answer, and they are filtered here. A dumb server answers with the
plain `info/refs` file, which has no `HEAD`.

A trailing `/` of `url` is removed. When the first request is redirected, the second goes to
the URL where the first one ended. The references are in the order of the server: `HEAD`
first, then by name.

#### Errors

- `GitRefError.NotGitRepository` if the answer is not a reference advertisement.
- `GitRefError.Malformed` if the advertisement is broken.
- `GitRefError.ServerError` if the server answers with an `ERR` packet.
- `GitRefError.Unsupported` if a version 2 server does not offer `ls-refs`.
- `HttpError` if a request fails, or the status is not from 200 to 299.
- `OutOfMemoryError` if the `Allocator` fails.

<a id="GitRemote.impl.parseAdvertisement"></a>

### Associated function `parseAdvertisement`

```silk
pub effect fn parseAdvertisement(body: &[u8], prefixes: &[String]) -> RefList
    ! GitRefError | OutOfMemoryError
    ? &mut Allocator
```

Returns the references of a version 0 or version 1 advertisement in `body` whose names start
with one of `prefixes`, or all of them when `prefixes` is empty.

#### Details

`body` is the answer to `GET <url>/info/refs?service=git-upload-pack` or the start of the
output of `git-upload-pack`: an optional `# service=` packet and flush, an optional
`version 1` packet, then one packet for each reference, and a flush. The first reference has
the capabilities after a NUL byte. A `symref=HEAD:<target>` capability sets the target of
`HEAD`, and a line `<id> <name>^{}` sets the peeled object of the reference before it. An
empty repository advertises no references, and the result then has only an unborn `HEAD` when
the server reports its target.

#### Errors

- `GitRefError.Malformed` if a packet or a line is broken.
- `GitRefError.ServerError` if the body has an `ERR` packet.
- `OutOfMemoryError` if the `Allocator` fails.

<a id="GitRemote.impl.parseLsRefs"></a>

### Associated function `parseLsRefs`

```silk
pub effect fn parseLsRefs(body: &[u8], prefixes: &[String]) -> RefList
    ! GitRefError | OutOfMemoryError
    ? &mut Allocator
```

Returns the references in `body`, the answer of a version 2 server to an `ls-refs` command,
whose names start with one of `prefixes`, or all of them when `prefixes` is empty.

#### Details

Each packet is `<id> <name>`, then optional `symref-target:<target>` and `peeled:<id>`
attributes, and a flush ends the list. A line that starts with `unborn` instead of an id is a
symbolic reference whose target does not exist yet, so its `id` is `None`.

#### Errors

- `GitRefError.Malformed` if a packet or a line is broken.
- `GitRefError.ServerError` if the body has an `ERR` packet.
- `OutOfMemoryError` if the `Allocator` fails.

<a id="GitRemote.impl.parseDumbRefs"></a>

### Associated function `parseDumbRefs`

```silk
pub effect fn parseDumbRefs(body: &[u8], prefixes: &[String]) -> RefList
    ! GitRefError | OutOfMemoryError
    ? &mut Allocator
```

Returns the references in `body`, the `info/refs` file of a dumb HTTP server, whose names
start with one of `prefixes`, or all of them when `prefixes` is empty.

#### Details

Each line is `<id>`, a tab, and the name, and ends with LF. A line whose name ends with `^{}`
sets the peeled object of the reference before it. The file has no `HEAD`.

#### Errors

- `GitRefError.NotGitRepository` if a line is not an id, a tab, and a name, for example in an
  HTML page.
- `OutOfMemoryError` if the `Allocator` fails.
